Read fixed-width ASCII file using SAS Setup file

Source: R/sas.R
sas_ascii_reader.Rd

sas_ascii_reader() and spss_ascii_reader() are used when you need to read a fixed-width ASCII (text) file that comes with a setup file. These file combinations are sometimes referred to as .txt+.sps, .txt+.sas, .dat+.sps, or .dat+.sas. The setup file provides instructions on how to create and name the columns, and fix the key-value pairs (sometimes called value labels). This is common in government data, particularly data produced before 2010.

Usage

sas_ascii_reader(
  dataset_name,
  sas_name,
  value_label_fix = TRUE,
  real_names = TRUE,
  keep_columns = NULL,
  coerce_numeric = TRUE,
  missing_values = c("all", "active", "none")
)

Arguments

dataset_name

Name of the ASCII (.txt) file that contains the data. This file may be zipped with a file extension of .zip.

sas_name

Name of the SAS Setup file - should be a .sas or .txt file.

value_label_fix

If TRUE, fixes value labels of the data. e.g. If a column is "sex" and has values of 0 or 1, and the setup file says 0 = male and 1 = female, it will make that change.

real_names

If TRUE fixes column names from default column name in the SPSS setup file (e.g. V1, V2) to the name it says the column is called (e.g. age, sex, etc.).

keep_columns

Specify which columns from the dataset you want. If NULL, will return all columns. Accepts the column number (e.g. 1:5), column name (e.g. V1, V2, etc.) or column label (e.g. VICTIM_NAME, CITY, etc.).

coerce_numeric

If TRUE (default) will make columns where all values can be made numeric into numeric columns. Every value is checked, so a column with any text value stays character. Useful as FALSE if variables have leading zeros - such as US Census FIPS codes. See read_ascii_setup for how implied decimal places are handled.

missing_values

Which of the setup file's missing values to set to NA. Setup files often have their missing values section commented out (e.g. "* MISSING VALUES" in SPSS or inside /* */ in SAS) so that the codes stay in the data unless the user chooses otherwise.

"all"

(default) Use every missing value in the setup file, ignoring whether it is commented out. This is what earlier versions did.

"active"

Use only the missing values that aren't commented out, as SPSS and SAS would.

"none"

Don't use any missing values; every code is kept.

Missing values are matched by value, as in SPSS and SAS, so a missing value written 9 also matches 09 or 0000009 in the data, except in columns the setup file says are text (SPSS "(A)", SAS "$"), where it must be the same text. Value labels are applied first, so a missing value that also has a value label (e.g. 9 = "Unknown") keeps its label rather than becoming NA unless use_value_labels = FALSE.

Value

Data.frame of the data from the ASCII file

Details

sas_ascii_reader() gives the same result as read_ascii_setup, which reads both SPSS and SAS setup files; its arguments just have older names.

See also

read_ascii_setup, spss_ascii_reader For using an SPSS setup file

Other ASCII Reader functions: spss_ascii_reader()

Examples

# Text file is zipped to save space.
dataset_name <- system.file("extdata", "example_data.zip",
  package = "asciiSetupReader")
sas_name <- system.file("extdata", "example_setup.sas",
  package = "asciiSetupReader")

example <- sas_ascii_reader(dataset_name = dataset_name,
  sas_name = sas_name)

# Only returns the first 5 columns
example2 <- sas_ascii_reader(dataset_name = dataset_name,
  sas_name = sas_name, keep_columns = 1:5)
